Seminar Title:

Identification, Functional Validation, and Therapeutic Targeting of Liver Fibrosis-Associated Genes Using Genome Editing and Novel Anti-Fibrotic Phytocompounds

Seminar Type:

Department:

Venue:

Date and Time:

Gajanan Bhujangrao Kendre

Abstract:

Fibrosis is a progressive pathological condition characterized by excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix proteins in response to chronic injury or damage, leading to organ dysfunction and ultimately organ failure. The normal wound-healing process and fibrogenic disease share similar mechanisms however, suppression of myofibroblasts following injury is impaired by epigenetic modifications of genes, leading to prolonged myofibroblast activation. Liver fibrosis is caused by various factors, including viral hepatitis, NAFLD, and metabolic disorders. This abundant fibrous stroma forms a microenvironment that supports tumour initiation and can lead to hepatocellular carcinoma. Therefore, the identification of gene biomarkers across heterogeneous datasets of fibrotic, HCV, cirrhosis, and HBV remains essential. Additionally, effective phytochemical therapeutic strategies for the treatment of liver fibrosis remain limited. This study aims to identify key fibrosis-associated genes and effective anti-fibrotic phytochemical candidates, and to explore their potential relevance in in vitro and in vivo liver fibrosis models. Publicly available datasets from GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) were analysed to identify differentially expressed genes. The prevalence and genetic variants of the key identified genes RNF7, RNF43, and OAS1 will be validated in the Indian population to understand their potential contribution to liver fibrosis. Despite the high prevalence of liver fibrosis, there are currently no approved therapies, likely due to the complexity of the condition and its late-stage diagnosis. Various phytocompounds with reported hepatoprotective effects and traditional associations with liver disease were analysed through in silico docking, and one phytocompound, Boeravinone B, was subsequently evaluated for its anti-fibrotic potential. The findings of this study are expected to provide novel genetic markers in the Indian population and a plant-derived therapeutic strategy for the treatment and prevention of liver fibrosis.
